irp.title: 2026 Integrated Resource Plan (Final) and Programmatic EIS
irp.regulator: TVA Board of Directors (self-regulated federal utility; no state commission docket)
irp.status_note: Board approved IRP recommendations at Aug 20, 2026 board meeting. Draft was released Sept 2024 as the '2025 IRP'; renamed 2026 IRP; preliminary final released June 2026.

load.energy_growth_note: Reference scenario energy 174,586 GWh (2026) -> 197,704 GWh (2036). IRP text: Reference load growth ~0.8%/yr avg; High Growth ~1.4%/yr; Carbon Legislation ~0.5%/yr. Peak CAGR 2026-2050: ~0.7% Reference, ~1.3% High Growth (2050 annual peak 39,451 MW Reference; 46,498 MW High Growth). TVA says actual/forecast demand has moved above the draft IRP Reference case and is 'approaching the Higher Growth Economy scenario primarily due to data center growth'. Peak growth % computed from Reference annual peak table (2026->2036).
load.large_load_notes: IRP gives no data-center MW figure; it says industrial growth is 'primarily data center'. Secondary (TVA Q1 FY26 earnings call, Feb 2026): data centers were 18% of TVA industrial load in 2025 and TVA projects data-center growth to double in its region by 2030. Winter peak records: 35,319 MW (Jan 2025, per Utility Dive). Aug 2026 board created a new data-center wholesale rate class. Named projects in IRP: Kairos Hermes (Gen IV reactor) in Oak Ridge; Type One Energy 'Infinity Two' fusion pilot at the former Bull Run site; Clinch River SMR site (Oak Ridge). No named data-center customers/locations in the IRP.

generation_adds.note: Reference scenario/Baseline strategy (portfolio 1A) incremental summer net dependable capacity by 2040. Range across all cases 4-13 GW. In progress: ~2 GW of CC being added by 2028.
Portfolio 1A by 2040. Range 3-13 GW. In progress: ~2 GW of frame and aero CT capacity by 2028.

Portfolio 1A 'renewables' by 2040 (summer net dependable). Range 2-5 GW SND = 3-12 GW nameplate. 3 GW nameplate of Green Invest/self-directed/Generation Flexibility solar contracted to come online by 2030. Wind additions suspended.
Portfolio 1A storage by 2040. Range 1-5 GW SND (1-8 GW nameplate). 0.7 GW of contracted battery projects online by 2030; pumped storage option being evaluated.

Clinch River Unit 1 BWRX-300 SMR, Oak Ridge TN; NRC construction permit issued Sept 2026. IRP range: up to 5 GW new nuclear by 2040 (Innovation strategy); Reference/Baseline portfolio adds ~0 nuclear by 2040.
Energy efficiency 1-2 GW and demand response up to 2 GW (DR used to 'enable interconnection of new industrial loads'). Total incremental capacity need 11-32 GW through 2040 across scenarios.

load.energy_growth_note: Winter-peaking system. Net energy 15.4 -> 18.4 million MWh (1.3%/yr, 2025-2039). Winter peak +416 MW (0.8%/yr), summer peak +411 MW (1.1%/yr). Record peak 3,754 MW (Jan 17, 2024). Base-year peak is the 2024-25 winter value in Table 3-2; end value is 2038-39 winter. 7% reserve margin now applied to winter and summer.
load.large_load_notes: The IRP base forecast EXCLUDES data centers and 'megaloads' (>450 MW); data centers are to be served separately under Rate DCP (approved Oct 30, 2025, Case 2025-00140; dedicated resources required above 250 MW). The 1,680 MW figure is NOT from the IRP: it is EKPC's July 16, 2026 RFP to serve a Deca Digital hyperscale data-center load ramping 27 MW (summer 2027) -> 200 -> 600 -> 1,000 -> 1,400 -> 1,680 MW (winter 2029/30). Site not named in the RFP; trade/local press report DECA proposing a ~$4B data center in Carroll County, KY (link to the EKPC RFP is an inference). EKPC also publicly supported a proposed data center near Spurlock Station, Maysville/Mason County (Dec 2025 planning-commission comments). In response to PSC staff, EKPC modeled a hypothetical 1 GW, 95% load-factor load: least-cost answer was two additional 745 MW 2x1 F-class NGCC units.

load.energy_growth_note: Preliminary LTLF peak: ~112,000 MW (2026), 278,003 MW (2029), 367,790 MW (2032) - driven overwhelmingly by TSP-reported large loads. Reality check: new unofficial all-time peak 91,134 MW on Jul 22, 2026 (prior record 85,508 MW, Aug 2023); ERCOT had projected summer 2026 peak of 90,500-98,000 MW. Alternative 'historical realization' adjustment (32% cut to data-center/crypto) would give ~168 GW (2029) and ~201 GW (2032). Growth % is computed from LTLF 2026->2032 values and is not credible as a planning number; it shows forecast inflation.
load.large_load_notes: Large Load Interconnection (LLI) requests: ~410 GW as of Mar 26, 2026 (~87% data centers; +178 GW since end-2025); 438 GW by May 2026; third-party tracker shows 466 GW (90% data centers) for Aug 2026. Batch Zero (one-time transitional study, loads >=75 MW): conditional classification Sept 3, 2026 - 204 projects / 66.4 GW base load and 158 projects / 127.9 GW studied load; 373 projects / 302.2 GW excluded. Governor Abbott's Aug 3, 2026 directive: ERCOT paused approvals to energize data centers and crypto facilities >=75 MW pending a verification audit; final Batch Zero classifications in December; Batch Zero study originally due Apr 9, 2027; Batch 1 targeted ~June 2027. Permian Basin load (oil & gas) forecast 23.7-26.4 GW drives 765 kV build.

rfp_or_procurement: No IRP-style procurement: energy-only market. Gas additions supported by Texas Energy Fund loans (slow progress per trade press). For large loads, the gating process is ERCOT's Batch Zero / Batch 1 study (Batch 1 ~June 2027), now subject to a state verification audit and an energization pause for data centers >=75 MW (since Aug 2026). Senate Bill 6 (2025) curtailment provisions apply to large loads.
headline: ERCOT's preliminary forecast (367,790 MW by 2032, about 4x today's 91 GW record) is inflated by a 410-466 GW large-load queue that is ~90% data centers; regulators are cutting it to a Batch Zero view (66 GW base / 128 GW studied) due in December 2026, while a 765 kV backbone (Permian import paths plus the $9.4B Eastern Backbone) is the big transmission build.
